See also: Pompa, pòmpa, pompă, and pompą

Esperanto

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

pompo +‎ -a

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpompa/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ompa
  • Syllabification: pom‧pa

Adjective

[edit]

pompa (accusative singular pompan, plural pompaj, accusative plural pompajn)

  1. pompous, showy, splendid
    Coordinate terms: brila, grandioza, solena
    pompa palaco, urbo, ceremonio ― pompous palace, city, ceremony

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pompa”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “pompa”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-2026

pompa

Hungarian

Pronunciation

  • Hyphenation: pom‧pa

Noun

pompa (plural pompák)

  1. pomp, splendour, luxury, magnificence

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Dutch pompe, pompen. Doublet of bomba.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Indonesian) IPA(key): /ˈpɔmpa/ [ˈpom.pa]
  • Rhymes: -ɔmpa
  • Syllabification: pom‧pa

Noun

[edit]

pompa (plural pompa-pompa)

  1. pump, a device for moving or compressing a liquid or gas
  2. (Medan slang) This term needs a translation to English. Please help out and add a translation, then remove the text {{rfdef}}.

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpom.pa/
  • Rhymes: -ompa
  • Hyphenation: póm‧pa

Etymology 1

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

pompa f (plural pompe)

  1. pump
  2. (sex, vulgar) blowjob
    Synonyms: bocchino, pompino
    Solo una pompa e via.
    Just a blowjob and that's it.
  3. pomp
Synonyms
[edit]
  • gala
  • pompa magna
  • suntuosità
  • magnificenza
Derived terms
[edit]
  • pompe funebri
  • pompare
Descendants
[edit]
  • → Amharic: ቧምቧ (bʷambʷa), ቧንቧ (bʷanbʷa)
  • → Ottoman Turkish: پومپا (pompa), پونپا (pompa)
    • Turkish: pompa
    • → Armenian: փոմփա (pʻompʻa)

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

pompa

  1. inflection of pompare:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Anagrams

[edit]

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Ancient Greek πομπή (pompḗ, “a sending, a solemn procession, pomp”), from πέμπω (pémpō, “to send”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈpɔm.pa]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈpɔm.pa]

Noun

[edit]

pompa f (genitive pompae); first declension

  1. procession, parade
  2. pomp

Declension

[edit]

First-declension noun.

singular plural
nominative pompa pompae
genitive pompae pompārum
dative pompae pompīs
accusative pompam pompās
ablative pompā pompīs
vocative pompa pompae

Descendants

[edit]
Descendants
  • Catalan: pompa
  • Esperanto: pompo
  • French: pompe
  • Galician: pompa
  • Hungarian: pompa
  • Italian: pompa
  • Portuguese: pompa
  • Sicilian: pompa
  • Spanish: pompa

References

[edit]
  • “pompa”, in Charlton T. Lewis and Charles Short (1879), A Latin Dictionary, Oxford: Clarendon Press
  • “pompa”, in Charlton T. Lewis (1891), An Elementary Latin Dictionary, New York: Harper & Brothers
  • "pompa", in Charles du Fresne du Cange, Glossarium Mediæ et Infimæ Latinitatis (augmented edition with additions by D. P. Carpenterius, Adelungius and others, edited by Léopold Favre, 1883–1887)
  • “pompa”, in Gaffiot, Félix (1934), Dictionnaire illustré latin-français, Hachette.
  • Carl Meißner; Henry William Auden (1894), Latin Phrase-Book‎[1], London: Macmillan and Co.
    • a funeral procession: pompa funebris
    • fine, rhetorical phrases: flosculi, rhetorum pompa
  • William Dwight Whitney, Benjamin E[li] Smith, editors (1911), “pomp”, in The Century Dictionary […], New York, N.Y.: The Century Co., →OCLC.

Spanish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpompa/ [ˈpõm.pa]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ompa
  • Syllabification: pom‧pa

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Latin pompa, from Ancient Greek πομπή (pompḗ, “sending, solemn procession, pomp”).

Noun

[edit]

pompa f (plural pompas)

  1. pomp
  2. boastfulness, ostentation, pageantry, glitz
  3. solemn procession
Derived terms
[edit]
  • pompa y circunstancia
  • pompas fúnebres
Related terms
[edit]
  • pomposo

Etymology 2

[edit]

Based on bomba.

Noun

[edit]

pompa f (plural pompas)

  1. bubble
    Synonym: burbuja
  2. pump
    Synonym: bomba
  3. (Mexico) buttock
    Synonyms: petacas, nalga
Derived terms
[edit]
  • pompa de jabón

Adjective

[edit]

pompa

  1. feminine singular of pompo

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pompa”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
